description.html: The red-green broadleaf artificial plant brings a warm color into the aquarium. The broad leaves shade from green to red, and the plant stands on a light-colored base, so it is easy to place without burying it.

An artificial plant does not wilt, needs no lighting or fertilizer and does not affect water parameters, so it is a good choice for beginners and for aquariums with fish that nibble or uproot live plants. It gives smaller fish, fry and shrimp cover and a place to rest.

The red leaves stand out best among green plants, in the middle of the aquarium, where they act as an accent. You can partly cover the base with sand or gravel to make it look more natural. During regular maintenance, take the plant out and rinse it with lukewarm water, removing algae with a soft brush and no detergents. Rinse it before putting it in the aquarium for the first time as well. Browse our other decorations and equipment.
